# EnterpriseGlue v0.35.4 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.35.3`.

## Highlights

- **engines:** Keep externally managed engines readable in the authorization-filtered engine inventory after workload registration.

## User and administrator impact

- Connected managed engines can appear in engine selectors and project deployment targets.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Upgrade the host packages or application images together; existing managed engine records require no repair.

## API and integration compatibility

- Engine response schemas accept the existing external_managed ownership mode while ordinary engine write requests remain unchanged.

## Database migrations

- Persistence and tenant ownership are unchanged. Downgrading restores the previous inventory validation failure for managed engines.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- Existing authorization, tenant filtering, secret redaction and workload ownership controls remain enforced.

## Documentation

- docs/reference/tenant-workload-lifecycle-api.md

## Rollback

- Revert to the previous qualified host composition; existing records remain intact.

## Validation evidence

- 140 affected schema, HTTP inventory, workload service and workload route tests passed.
- 21 engine selector and project deployment-target UI tests passed.
- Engine-tenancy and OpenAPI contracts passed, including managed ownership response and write-boundary assertions.
- Native ARM64 PostgreSQL managed registration/replay/decommission integration passed with the real persisted row projected into the inventory contract.
- Shared, backend-host and frontend-host builds, application typechecks, package version discipline, plugin API compatibility and documentation boundary checks passed.
